title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
subtitle: thick, chewy cookies with pools of dark chocolate
excerpt: These cookies have crisp edges and a soft, fudgy centre. Brown sugar and a little extra yolk give them chew. Use good dark chocolate -- either chips or a bar chopped roughly so you get shards of different sizes throughout.
sourceNotes: The chocolate chip cookie originates in the US. This version is adapted for the British preference for a less sweet, more chocolatey result.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze raw dough balls. Bake from frozen adding 2 minutes to the time.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe. Freeze half the dough for baking later.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough can rest in the fridge for up to 3 days before baking. The longer the rest, the more flavourful.

content.text: Take the cookies out of the oven when they look underdone. The centres should still appear slightly raw and glossy. They will set as they cool on the hot tray. If they look done in the oven, they will be hard when cold.

items.prepNote: plus 1 extra yolk -- the yolk adds chew
use 200g dark chocolate chips or a bar roughly chopped

content.text: Beat the softened butter with both sugars until pale and fluffy -- about 3 minutes. Beat in the egg, extra yolk, and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, and salt until a dough forms. Fold in the chocolate pieces.
If time allows, cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (or up to 3 days). Cold dough produces thicker cookies.
Heat the oven to 180C. Line two baking sheets. Roll the dough into balls about the size of a golf ball (roughly 40g each). Place with plenty of space -- they will spread.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until the edges are set and golden but the centres still look slightly glossy. Leave on the tray for 10 minutes before moving.

items.symptom: Cookies spread too thin and are crispy throughout
items.cause: Butter was too warm, or dough was not chilled.
items.fix: Make sure the dough is cold before baking. If the kitchen is warm, chill shaped balls for 20 minutes before baking.

items.symptom: Cookies are cakey rather than chewy
items.cause: Too much flour, or the egg white ratio was too high.
items.fix: Measure flour by spooning into the cup or weighing. Use the egg plus extra yolk -- the white adds lift and makes the texture cakey.

content.text: Chocolate chip cookies were created in the US in 1938 and arrived in British home kitchens in the 1980s and 90s. They have since become one of the most baked things in British home kitchens. The American original was sweet and soft; the British version tends to lean darker and less sweet. Both are correct. These are the weekend biscuit.
